nodes.label: lithe
nodes.rationale: A bare-bones code editor in Rust, local only: no account, no telemetry, no network, no LLM. Code editing, LSP, search, version control, and nothing else.

nodes.label: Hand-rolled wgpu text renderer
nodes.rationale: Chosen over a UI toolkit because a code editor is a character grid and that fact is worth exploiting.

nodes.label: Two render primitives: rect and text
nodes.rationale: Editor body, gutter, file tree, command palette, search results and status bar are all the same two calls at different coordinates - one instanced draw per frame against one glyph atlas. There is no widget tree.

nodes.label: Mac app bundle (scripts/bundle.sh)
nodes.rationale: A bare binary run from a terminal is only half an app to macOS: unreliable menu bar, executable name in the Dock, no icon. The bundle adds an Info.plist, a generated icon and an ad-hoc signature, which is what makes the native menu behave.

nodes.label: Native menu bar (File, Edit, Go, View)
nodes.rationale: Exists so the shortcuts are discoverable rather than folklore; Open File, Open Folder and Save As use the system dialogs.

nodes.label: Landing page
nodes.rationale: Launched with no argument: New buffer, Open file, Open folder, New window, and recently opened projects. Every row is clickable, and the status-bar panel toggles stay clickable here because that is when you are most likely to reach for one.

nodes.label: Fuzzy open (cmd+P)
nodes.rationale: Keeps paths and never file contents, and only builds that list when you first press cmd+P. This is the main reason mainstream editors idle at a gigabyte and this one does not.

nodes.label: Three design invariants
nodes.rationale: Redraw only on damage, lay out only what is visible, no index of our own - stated in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md as the invariants every feature has to respect.

nodes.label: Context menus built per click
nodes.rationale: Two menus, built per click from what is actually actionable - an entry that would quietly do nothing is not offered. LSP entries need a server for the language; git entries need the project to be a repository.

nodes.label: Copy Permalink to Line
nodes.rationale: Builds a link to the current commit on GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket, and says it cannot rather than guessing at an unknown host.

nodes.label: Rename Symbol
nodes.rationale: Asks for the new name, then applies the server's workspace edit - to open buffers as an undoable change, and to closed files directly on disk.

nodes.label: References and call lists fill the search panel
nodes.rationale: Find All References and the two call lists reuse the search panel so they scroll and click through the same way a project search does.

nodes.label: Preview for Markdown, SVG and images
nodes.rationale: Each kind opens either rendered or as its source and remembers which you chose; Markdown defaults to its source, SVG and images to the picture. A file that is not text opens as an image or a note saying so, and is never written back over.

nodes.label: SVG has its own preview switch
nodes.rationale: SVG is the one picture format that is also a text file worth editing: turning its preview off shows the markup, while doing the same to a PNG would show an empty buffer.

nodes.label: HTML has no preview
nodes.rationale: It had one and it was never what anyone wanted: a reader that understands the structural tags but no stylesheet, script or layout shows a document nothing on the web would render that way. Inline HTML inside Markdown is still read.

nodes.label: Markdown preview reader
nodes.rationale: Headings, paragraphs, emphasis, code, all three link kinds, lists, checkboxes, quotes, rules, pipe tables, hidden YAML front matter and inline HTML. One font at one size, so structure is carried by weight and colour; fenced code is highlighted by the editor's own tree-sitter grammars, and a fence naming an uninstalled language stays plain rather than being coloured by a guess.

nodes.label: Unknown HTML tags left as written
nodes.rationale: Left as written rather than dropped, because Vec<T> in prose is commoner in a code editor's README than hand-written HTML.

nodes.label: Images named, not drawn, in Markdown
nodes.rationale: A picture inside flowed text would mean laying out rows of unequal height around it, and for the badges at the top of a README the name is all there was to say.

nodes.label: Self-opening completion list
nodes.rationale: Opens on a character the server names as a trigger and after two characters of a word. One request per word, not one per keystroke: once the list is open, further typing narrows what it already has, which costs nothing and needs no round trip. Accepting one replaces the typed word rather than following it.

nodes.label: Hover (400ms dwell, cmd+I)
nodes.rationale: The answer is drawn as a small document because a server sends Markdown, and a signature arrives as a highlighted code block. Nothing is asked unless a server for that language is already running: resting a pointer must not start a process.

nodes.label: Initialize Repository
nodes.rationale: Offered instead of an empty list of changes, which reads as 'nothing has changed'. It shells out to git init, so the result is the repository git would have made: its hooks, its default branch name, its templates.

nodes.label: Line blame (cmd+shift+B)
nodes.rationale: One git blame per file, not per line: the annotation follows the caret and spawning a subprocess every time you press Down is not something this editor is allowed to do. Commits are stored once and referenced per line, so a ten-thousand-line file is forty kilobytes rather than ten thousand strings. A modified buffer says 'unsaved changes', because blame reads the file on disk and a confident wrong name is worse than none.

nodes.label: Editable side-by-side diff
nodes.rationale: Side by side by default because two columns is what a diff looks like everywhere else. Its right-hand column is the buffer, read from the buffer rather than from disk so an edit shows up as it is typed; it opens in that file's own tab marked with a plus-minus because the diff and the buffer are one thing.

nodes.label: Commit diff is read only
nodes.rationale: A diff opened from History has no buffer behind it, so it says read only and means it, and clicking through a history reuses one tab rather than leaving one per commit.

nodes.label: settings.toml records only changes
nodes.rationale: Writing every value would freeze the defaults at the moment the file was first written: toggling one preference would record all the others as though they had been decided, and changing a default afterwards could never reach anyone who had the file. A malformed file falls back to defaults rather than refusing to start.

nodes.label: A tab is not always a file
nodes.rationale: Settings and diffs are things you open, look at and close, which is what a tab is for. As modes drawn over the editor they hid the file you were working on and the only way back was the shortcut that opened them; there is only ever one settings tab however many times you ask.

nodes.label: File tree context menu
nodes.rationale: New File/Folder, Reveal in Finder, Open in Default App or Terminal, Cut/Copy/Duplicate/Paste, Undo/Redo, Copy Path, Rename, Move to Trash, Delete. Right-clicking empty space acts on the project root.

nodes.label: In-place naming in the tree
nodes.rationale: New File, New Folder and Rename are typed on the row where the result will appear. A name is a name: one containing a path separator is refused rather than silently writing somewhere else, and an existing file is never overwritten.

nodes.label: File clipboard with its own undo
nodes.rationale: The path also goes on the system clipboard so it is not a black hole. Undo and Redo take back what the menu did to the filesystem; Move to Trash is recoverable and is what Undo reverses, while Delete is not, so it is the one entry that asks first.

nodes.label: Source control panel (changes and history)
nodes.rationale: changes stages and unstages, history lists recent commits. git status runs when something could have changed it, not every frame. Clicking a file shows its unified diff against HEAD with long unchanged runs elided; clicking again opens it for editing.

nodes.label: View File History (--follow)
nodes.rationale: Narrows the history tab to the commits that touched one file, with --follow so a rename does not cut it short; clicking the History tab widens it back to the project.

nodes.label: Autosave
nodes.rationale: Writes a modified buffer back after a pause in typing and when the window loses focus. Only buffers that have a path: inventing a filename for a scratch buffer would be worse than leaving it unsaved. It goes through the same temp-file-and-rename path a manual save does.

nodes.label: Temp-file-and-rename save
nodes.rationale: Saving goes through a temp file and a rename so an interrupted write cannot truncate your code; closing with unsaved edits asks first, in a native dialog.

nodes.label: Single-click preview tab
nodes.rationale: Clicking a file in the tree opens it in a preview tab drawn dimmer, and the next single click reuses that slot, so browsing twenty files leaves one tab rather than twenty. Double-clicking it, or typing in it, makes it permanent.

nodes.label: Fractional scrolling
nodes.rationale: Fractional rather than line-by-line, because a trackpad sends pixel deltas and rounding each one to a whole line is what makes scrolling feel like it is catching.

nodes.label: Recent projects file
nodes.rationale: One plain text file, one absolute path per line, under Application Support or XDG_CONFIG_HOME. No database, nothing to migrate, and you can edit it in the editor. Writing it re-reads first and merges, since several windows each hold their own copy and a stale write would drop whatever another added.

nodes.label: Opening a folder replaces the project
nodes.rationale: Rather than merging into it: two projects' files in one tree is never what was meant.

nodes.label: Independent windows sharing one GPU device
nodes.rationale: Each window owns its project root, open buffers and file tree, so a second window can sit on a different repository. They share one wgpu device and one rasterised glyph atlas, which is why a second window costs five megabytes rather than twenty - the font system behind the atlas is eight on its own.

nodes.label: Measured, not asserted
nodes.rationale: macOS 27 / Apple M5 release figures: 0.000% idle CPU, 13 us of document work per frame independent of file size, a 143 MB 3M-line file open in 0.05 s, 11.8 ms worst-case fuzzy keystroke over 200,000 paths, 0.26 ms mean keystroke reparse. The floor is the platform's: 63 MB of AppKit before a line of our code runs, where Electron-based editors idle between 500 MB and 1 GB.

nodes.label: Incremental parsing
nodes.rationale: An edit is described to the tree before the reparse, so a keystroke costs a fraction of a millisecond instead of re-parsing the file. The parser reads the rope in chunks and never flattens it into a String.

nodes.label: Viewport-bounded highlight query
nodes.rationale: The highlight query is restricted to the visible byte range, so colouring a three-million-line file costs what colouring a short one does - measured at 97 us per frame.

nodes.label: Highlighting switched off above 2 MB
nodes.rationale: A parse tree is about 26x the source it describes, so highlighting stops above 2 MB; past that a file still opens instantly, just uncoloured.

nodes.label: Undo discards the tree and reparses
nodes.rationale: Rather than deriving inverse edits: ~16 ms on a 14,000-line file, fine for a keypress and visible if you hold the key down.

nodes.label: tree-sitter grammars, nine languages
nodes.rationale: Rust, TypeScript, TSX, JavaScript, Python, Go, C, JSON and TOML; the nine grammars are about 6 MB of the 12 MB stripped binary.

nodes.label: Adding a language is a dependency and a row
nodes.rationale: Adding one is a dependency and a row in crates/syntax/src/languages.rs - the language set is table-driven rather than wired through code paths.

nodes.label: Search on ripgrep's engine
nodes.rationale: Uses ripgrep's own grep-regex and grep-searcher so in-buffer find means exactly what project search means: one pattern syntax, one set of case rules. Project search streams, the previous worker is cancelled when you retype, and the result set is capped because a result list is the closest thing to an index we keep.

nodes.label: Language server lifecycle and probing
nodes.rationale: One process per language, started on the first buffer that needs it and killed on exit. A candidate that spawns and then exits within 250 ms is treated as broken and the next is tried, because being on PATH is not enough: rust-analyzer there is often a rustup proxy for a component never installed. The status bar names the state and asking a missing server names the command that installs it.

nodes.label: Whole-document LSP sync
nodes.rationale: Coalesced to one send per frame. Incremental sync would send less but has to agree with the server about UTF-16 ranges on every edit, and a single disagreement desynchronises it silently for the rest of the session.

nodes.label: UTF-16 column counting
nodes.rationale: LSP counts columns in UTF-16 code units, which is tested round-trip through emoji and CJK.

nodes.label: Git splits by direction
nodes.rationale: Reads are gitoxide because the gutter runs on every frame and must never stall on a subprocess. Writes shell out to git: gix 0.88 exposes commit() but no way to turn an index into a tree, so committing through it would mean building tree objects and moving refs by hand, and a bug there costs someone their work where a bug in the gutter costs a redraw. The tests check the result by asking git log rather than asking ourselves.

nodes.label: gitoxide (gix) for reads
nodes.rationale: HEAD blobs and line diff in-process, so the gutter and the diff against HEAD never spawn anything; the diff is recomputed only when the file or its revision changes.

nodes.label: git CLI for writes
nodes.rationale: Staging, committing, init and blame shell out: these are one-off actions a person asks for and git is the reference implementation.

nodes.label: Offscreen pixel tests
nodes.rationale: A hand-rolled text renderer fails in ways a type checker cannot see, so the renderer can draw to an offscreen texture and the tests read the pixels back. The render tests skip rather than fail where there is no GPU.

nodes.label: --snapshot frame capture
nodes.rationale: Renders one frame to raw RGBA, optionally with an overlay such as the picker up, so a frame can be inspected outside a live window.

nodes.label: LITHE_TRACE event logging
nodes.rationale: Logs every window event, which is what makes the redraw-on-damage invariant measurable rather than asserted.

nodes.label: Roadmap M1-M7 (all done)
nodes.rationale: the frame, the editor, files, syntax, search, lsp, vcs - each milestone ends at something usable.
